ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a square, and near each of the four corners there is an identical circle; each corner circle is tangent to the two adjacent sides of the square. Inside the upper-left corner circle there is a radius line and it is labeled as 1, indicating that the radii of these corner circles are 1. In the central region of the square there is a radius line labeled as 2, which, combined with the meaning of the problem, indicates that the middle circle has radius 2, and that it is externally tangent to the four corner circles. The figure is symmetric about the center of the square. Then reason: Let the side length of the square be s, and take the lower-left corner of the square as the origin, then the center of the square is (s/2, s/2). Since the circle of radius 1 at the corner is tangent to two adjacent sides at the same time, the center of the small circle in the lower-left corner is (1,1). The central circle has radius 2, and by symmetry its center is at the center of the square (s/2,s/2). The central circle and the small circle are externally tangent, so the distance between the centers of the two circles equals 2+1=3. Thus there is ((s/2)-1)^2+((s/2)-1)^2=3^2. That is, 2(s/2-1)^2=9, so s/2-1=3/sqrt(2)=3sqrt(2)/2, giving s=2+3sqrt(2). Therefore the area of the square is s^2=(2+3sqrt(2))^2=4+12sqrt(2)+18=22+12sqrt(2).
